item.title: CISA adds Ivanti EPMM unauthenticated remote code execution zero day CVE-2026-105192 to KEV catalog
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity authorities have expanded the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog under Binding Operational Directive 26-04 to mandate emergency mitigation for an actively weaponized enterprise mobility management flaw. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit malformed API parameters to execute arbitrary operating system commands with root privileges across mobile device management servers.
The catalog update features Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile EPMM unauthenticated command injection flaw CVE-2026-105192 carrying a CVSS score of 9.8. Threat telemetry confirms state-backed threat actors actively weaponizing the defect to achieve initial access, extract device registration databases, and push rogue configuration profiles to managed enterprise mobile endpoints. Under Binding Operational Directive 26-04, federal civilian executive branch agencies face an emergency October 17 compliance deadline to apply vendor security updates.
Subverting central enterprise mobility management platforms compromises whole-fleet device boundaries. Because EPMM servers issue device certificates, push mobile application payloads, and manage corporate network access credentials, an unauthenticated server takeover permits threat actors to compromise enrolled mobile endpoints, intercept internal communications, and pivot into corporate networks.
- Apply official maintenance security updates published by Ivanti across all Endpoint Manager Mobile appliances immediately. - Isolate EPMM web management interfaces behind zero trust access control proxies and enforce strict IP access control lists. - Inspect EPMM system execution logs for anomalous shell processes spawned by web server daemons or unverified API calls. - Audit enrolled mobile device inventories for unauthorized profile deployments or unverified administrative account additions.
Enterprise mobility management defense demands rapid patch execution and strict API control plane isolation to ensure mobile management infrastructure remains protected from unauthenticated command injection zero-days. #CodeDefence #Ivanti #EPMM #MobileSecurity #CISA #KEV #ZeroDay #RCE #AppSec

item.title: Sophos issues urgent advisories for max severity Firewall auth bypass flaw CVE-2026-106110 exploited in the wild
item.description:
Network security appliance maintainers have distributed hotfixes following active wild exploitation targeting edge firewall management interfaces. Remote adversaries manipulate session handling subroutines to bypass authentication controls and execute arbitrary code on firewall appliances.
The security advisory addresses authentication bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-106110 carrying a CVSS score of 9.8 in Sophos Firewall User Portal and Webadmin interfaces. Unauthenticated remote actors transmit malformed JSON Web Tokens containing manipulated key ID parameters to force the authentication engine into validating forged administrative sessions. Threat research disclosures confirm automated exploitation toolkits actively scanning exposed firewall portals to deploy persistent reverse shell implants.
Subverting edge firewall appliances destroys network perimeter boundary controls across enterprise subnets. Because Sophos Firewall appliances manage routing policies, intrusion prevention inspection rules, and site-to-site VPN tunnels, an unauthenticated administrative compromise allows threat actors to disable security filters, harvest network credentials, and execute lateral movement sweeps.
- Deploy hotfixes automatically or apply manual firmware updates published by Sophos across all managed Firewall appliances. - Disable public WAN access to User Portal and Webadmin interfaces, restricting administrative access to internal management VLANs. - Inspect firewall system access logs for anomalous JWT authentication assertions or unverified admin login events. - Reset administrative account credentials and invalidate active user session tokens across managed firewall fleets.
Perimeter firewall controller defense relies on strict management interface isolation and rapid hotfix deployment to ensure edge access gateways remain shielded from unauthenticated session forgery attacks. #CodeDefence #Sophos #Firewall #AuthBypass #PerimeterSecurity #NetworkSecurity #ZeroDay #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: SolarWinds patches critical Access Rights Manager remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-107220
item.description:
Enterprise identity auditing software maintainers have released security maintenance updates to address a high severity remote code execution vulnerability in access governance tools. Unauthenticated remote actors can exploit deserialization errors to execute commands under SYSTEM privileges.
The security update fixes deserialization vulnerability CVE-2026-107220 affecting SolarWinds Access Rights Manager ARM software installations. The defect resides within background RPC processing daemons handling administrative configuration requests. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit malformed serialized objects over port 55555 to trigger untrusted object deserialization, executing arbitrary operating system commands with SYSTEM privileges on the host server. Official security bulletins urge enterprise IT administrators to apply current fixed release builds.
Subverting access rights management servers exposes Active Directory authorization structures and enterprise identity records. Because ARM tools manage user provisioning, group policy audits, and Active Directory permissions, a host-level compromise permits threat actors to extract directory credentials and manipulate access control lists.
- Upgrade SolarWinds Access Rights Manager ARM installations immediately to official fixed release build 2026.4 or higher. - Restrict inbound network connectivity to ARM RPC management ports using internal host firewalls and network segmentation rules. - Inspect ARM server process trees for unauthorized shell invocations originating from the SolarWinds service daemon process. - Audit Active Directory administrative group memberships and access rights changes processed during recent management windows.
Identity auditing platform defense demands rigid input deserialization sanitization and strict RPC interface isolation to ensure access governance servers remain protected from unauthenticated remote command execution. #CodeDefence #SolarWinds #ARM #ActiveDirectory #IdentitySecurity #RCE #Deserialization #AppSec #PatchManagement
